[quote=alkiragunya;59346611]O conselho olha para Djalu, Tjarrampa é o primeiro a responder.
[i]Enviar Ngankaris para seu país, e isso?[/i]
Balunji procede para explicar o termo.
[I]Ngankaris são indivíduos responsáveis pelo tratamento de doenças e contar histórias, transmitindo nosso conhecimento ao longo do tempo, em muitos milênios, talvez poderemos enviar alguns junto da caravana de camelos se assim desejarem, certamente seria algo....único.[/I]
Tjarrampa prossegue após Balunji terminar.
[i]E quanto a sua pergunta, sim , há cobre, em alguns depósitos do norte, o qual alguns clãs menores não representados no conselho tem controle e-[/i]
[I] isso é mentira , os Matuntaras mineram o cobre de lá e lucram vendendo esse cobre para outros clãs, eles são quem tem as únicas fontes de cobre em Alkiragunya.[/i]
Outro Ancião, até então calado disse.
[i]Mas é claro, podemos convencer eles a ceder parte desse cobre.[/i]
O homem mascarado até então observando quieto, mas focado diz.
[i]Os Matuntaras desistiram de seu cobre há séculos quando descobriram o ouro, bem mais abundante, há no entanto, alguns clãs que de fato mineram o cobre, clãs menores, e podemos convencer eles facilmente a ceder esse cobre sem incomodar os Matuntaras, é claro, esses clãs usam esse cobre para sobreviverem e criarem ferramentas...mas nada que um bom acordo não resolva[/i].
The council looks at Djalu, Tjarrampa is the first to respond.

[i]Send Ngankaris to your  country, and that's it?[/i]

Balunji proceeds to explain the term.

[i]Ngankaris are individuals responsible for treating illnesses and telling stories, passing on our knowledge over time, in many millennia, perhaps we could send some along with the camel caravan if they so wish, it would certainly be something... unique.[/i]

Tjarrampa continues after Balunji finishes.

[i]And as for your question, yes, there is copper, in some deposits in the north, which some smaller clans not represented in the council have control over and-
that's a lie, the Matuntaras mine the copper there and profit by selling it to other clans, they are the ones who have the only sources of copper in Alkiragunya.[/i]

Another Elder, until then silent, said.

[i]But of course, we can convince them to give up some of that copper.[/i]

The masked man, until then observing quietly, but focused, said.

[i]The Matuntaras gave up their copper centuries ago when they discovered gold, which is much more abundant. However, there are some clans that actually mine copper, smaller clans, and we can easily convince them to give up this copper without bothering the Matuntaras. Of course, these clans use this copper to survive and create tools...but nothing that a good deal can't solve.[/i][/quote]

The tall and silent Trym speaks up for the first time.
[i]If one of the main tings they use the copper for are tools and similar tings then we have someting to trade for it that would be of interest to them, Nordiheim is rich in iron and coal, and therfor have a triving steel industry that are capable of making many tings.[/i]

Olaf, while a little suprised that Trym suddenly said someting, quickly elaborate on what whas said.
[i]Be it iron or steel bars for forging, coal for fuel or joust tools and equipment made of steel, I feel confident that the Nordiheimian council would be glad to trade it for copper and camels without complaint[/i] 

[i]And if there are other tings that our two nations finds that they want to expand the trade with over time, that will always be an option to.[/i] Tau adds.
